Please review our <\/span>DLF Code of Conduct<\/span><\/a><\/span> prior to joining us at the Forum. On site, DLF staff will be identifiable by their name badges and white lanyards.<\/span><\/p>","_id":"9dfe99e"},{"tab_title":"For First-Time Attendees","tab_content":"

We hope our first-time attendees will feel empowered and comfortable when they attend our events. The DLF Community Committee typically plans social and newcomers\u2019 events - check the Wellness and Activities page for more information.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

Before the events:<\/strong><\/p>

  • When you register, consider signing up for the <\/span>DLF mentorship program<\/span><\/a><\/span>.\u00a0<\/span><\/li>
  • We encourage you to select or enter your pronouns to appear on your conference badge when you register and create your user account on our conference management system. This is an entirely optional field, and we welcome everyone to make a selection.<\/span><\/li>
  • There\u2019s no strict dress code at the Forum, but attendees tend to gravitate towards business casual attire. See photos from last year for a better idea<\/span>.<\/a> Additionally, meeting rooms can be chilly, so consider keeping a sweater or jacket on hand just in case.<\/span><\/li><\/ul>


    During the events:<\/strong><\/p>

    • All sessions at the Forum are open to anyone\u2014Working Group meetings (aka DLF Working Sessions) included. Please feel free to join these whether you\u2019re interested in joining group activities or just learning more about them.<\/span><\/li>
    • We are completely aware of how hard conferencing can be, and want you to have a good experience. Know it\u2019s ok to leave a session if it\u2019s not what you were expecting, or to miss one entirely because you\u2019re otherwise occupied or just need a break. There will be a designated Quiet Room onsite for anyone who wants to recharge or get some work done.<\/span><\/li>
    • Every session has a shared notes doc if you want to catch up on something you missed (or contribute for others), and presenters will be encouraged to upload slides to DLF\u2019s OSF repository. Links are available on the shared notes and slides page<\/a>.<\/span><\/li>
    • Have a question for organizers during the events? Let us know by stopping by the registration desk, stopping anyone with a white lanyard (which indicates staff), or emailing us at forum@diglib.org<\/span><\/a>.<\/span><\/li><\/ul>","_id":"4de920a"},{"tab_title":"Active Bystander Orientation","tab_content":"

      Have you ever witnessed bullying, harassment, or an uncomfortable encounter in a professional context and wished you knew how to intervene? It can be challenging to know what to say or do on the spot. The DLF Code of Conduct invites participants to be Active Bystanders, but what does that really mean?<\/span><\/p>

      DLF's Committee for Equity and Inclusion hosted an Active Bystander Orientation on October 24, 2023, ahead of the 2023 DLF Forum and affiliated events. This presentation provides an introduction to bystander intervention and an overview of strategies.<\/span><\/p>

      View the recording here<\/span>.<\/span><\/a><\/p>

      Slides are here<\/span>.<\/span><\/a><\/p>

      Suggested readings and resources are here<\/span>.<\/span><\/a><\/p>","_id":"f5fbad5"},{"_id":"163c63a","tab_title":"Transportation - Getting to East Lansing","tab_content":"

      The MSU campus is a 15-minute drive from <\/span>Capital Regional International Airport<\/span><\/a><\/span>. Taxicab service costs approximately $15.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

      It is a 75-minute (90 mile) drive from <\/span>Detroit Metro Airport<\/span><\/a><\/span>. The <\/span>Michigan Flyer Airport Shuttle<\/span><\/a><\/span> offers bus transportation to East Lansing for approximately $30. Buses run several times a day, and travel takes approximately two hours.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

      East Lansing is also accessible from the smaller <\/span>Gerald R. Ford International Airport<\/span><\/a><\/span> in Grand Rapids. It\u2019s a 60-minute (65 mile) drive between the two.<\/span><\/p>

      The <\/span>Capital Area Multimodal Gateway<\/span><\/a><\/span> on campus houses the <\/span>Amtrak Blue Water<\/span><\/a><\/span> train stop as well as <\/span>Greyhound<\/span><\/a><\/span> and <\/span>Indian Trails<\/span><\/a><\/span> bus services.<\/span><\/p>

      Local <\/span>CATA<\/span><\/a><\/span> (Capital Area Transportation Authority) bus routes stop at the station, and the facility also offers taxicab and bike-sharing services.<\/span><\/p>

      MSU campus transportation information<\/span><\/a><\/span> is also available, as is <\/span>information about campus safety<\/span><\/a><\/span>.<\/span><\/p>


      Parking at MSU<\/b><\/p>

      There are pay-by-plate lots or metered spaces around campus. Parking rates are $2 per hour. Check for more parking information at <\/span>MSU Police Parking Office Page<\/span><\/span><\/a> and <\/span>find visitor parking here<\/span><\/span><\/a>. Additionally, <\/span>information about complimentary parking at MSU is available here<\/span><\/a><\/span>. Accessible parking spaces are available to vehicles with the appropriate state-issued disability parking placard at any time.<\/span><\/p>

      MSU Main Library<\/b><\/p>

      Accessible parking for the library is located on the east side of the Main Library, and at the South (back) entrance. MSU Museum across the library also has an accessibility parking spot.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

      Wells Hall<\/b><\/p>

      Accessible parking spots for Wells Hall are located on Red Cedar Rd., the east side of Wells.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

      MSU Broad Art Museum<\/b><\/p>

      The nearest designated accessible parking spaces can be found directly south of the museum in Lot 8 (next to the Student Services building). Additional accessible parking areas can be found in the Grand River parking structure (<\/span>Ramp 6<\/span><\/a><\/span>), as well as north of Grand River Avenue in the City of East Lansing surface lots.<\/span><\/p>"},{"tab_title":"Health Protocols","tab_content":"

      While CLIR\/DLF will not be issuing event-specific health protocol announcements in 2024, we maintain and reinforce the following:<\/span><\/p>

      • Masking will be recommended but not required at the DLF Forum at Michigan State University.<\/span><\/li>
      • Our events will be mask-friendly, meaning anyone who wants to wear a mask will be welcome to do so, no questions asked.\u00a0<\/span><\/li>
      • CLIR will have masks, tests, and sanitizer available free of charge at the registration desk for anyone who needs them.<\/span><\/li>
      • Any harassment related to masking will be a violation of our <\/span>Code of Conduct<\/span><\/span><\/a> and may be reported and consequences enforced in the same way as any other CoC violation.<\/span><\/li>
      • CLIR will communicate promptly and transparently to all attendees if we learn of a positive test at the Forum.\u00a0<\/span><\/li>
      • CLIR will communicate these expectations openly and regularly to all prospective and registered attendees in the weeks leading up to the events.

        <\/span><\/li><\/ul>

        If you have questions, please send us an email at <\/span>forum@diglib.org<\/span><\/span><\/a>.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>","_id":"77e2470"},{"tab_title":"Emergency and Local Care Information","tab_content":"

        Should an emergency or otherwise unexpected serious disruption occur, please phone emergency services at 911 immediately. <\/span><\/p>\n

        DLF staff (who will be clearly designated for the duration of the Forum with name badges and white lanyards) will be onsite to assist by contacting hotel\/venue security or local law enforcement, providing escorts, or otherwise helping address the situation in the swiftest, most calm and organized way possible. <\/span><\/p>\n

        You can also reach CLIR\/DLF staff at our emergency\/Code of Conduct number at (732) 737-7328 (732-RESPECT) between 7am and 9pm local time. Outside of those hours, please contact the hotel or dial 911 for any after-hours emergencies.<\/span><\/p>\n

         <\/span><\/p>\n

        Hospitals near Michigan State University<\/b><\/p>\n

          \n
        • McLaren Greater Lansing Hospital Emergency Room<\/span><\/a><\/span> (3.7 miles away \/ 11 minute drive) - 2900 Collins Rd., Lansing, 48910. Phone: 517-975-7500.<\/span><\/li>\n
        • E.W. Sparrow Hospital Emergency Room<\/span><\/span><\/a> (3.7 miles away \/ 11 minute drive) - 1215 E. Michigan Ave., Lansing, 48912. Phone: 877-727-7691.<\/span><\/li>\n<\/ul>\n


          <\/b><\/p>

          Urgent care centers near Michigan State University<\/b><\/p>\n

          Please call or visit their websites to learn more about their limited hours. <\/span><\/p>\n

            \n
          • Sparrow Urgent Care<\/span><\/a><\/span> (2 miles away \/ 7 minute drive) - 2682 E. Grand River Ave., East Lansing, 48823. Phone: 517-333-6562<\/span><\/li>\n
          • Lansing Urgent Care - Frandor<\/span><\/a><\/span> (2.5 mile away \/ 9 minute drive) - 505 N. Clippert St., Lansing, 48912. Phone: 517-999-2273<\/span><\/li>\n<\/ul>","_id":"29925e2"},{"tab_title":"For Families","tab_content":"

            Nursing Room<\/b><\/p>

            We will provide a nursing room onsite for those who prefer a quiet, private place to breastfeed their baby or pump. However, please feed your baby whenever and wherever you like. We strive to be a friendly environment for families.<\/span><\/p>

            Please ask for the key to the nursing room at the conference registration desk. This room is accessible to one family at a time and is located in a private classroom room away from the conference spaces. The room has chairs and a table and is across the hallway from a kitchen and a bathroom.<\/span><\/p>

            Childcare and Summer Camp Options<\/b><\/p>

            While we are not able to provide onsite childcare at the DLF Forum this year, the planning team has compiled a list of resources that may help. Note that many childcare places near campus do not allow for drop ins, including Spartan Child Development Center and People\u2019s Church Preschool.<\/span><\/p>

            • Bailey Preschool<\/span><\/span><\/a>
              • $60-75 daily on a space-available basis.\u00a0<\/span><\/li>
              • Reservations need to be made at least two weeks in advance<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li>
              • Hannah Community Center School-age summer camps<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/li>
              • Launch Trampoline Park<\/span><\/a><\/span>: $35 day pass<\/span><\/li>
              • YMCA camps<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/li>
              • GymKind Gymnastics Camps<\/span><\/a><\/span> (in Meridian Mall in Okemos). Options during during the week of the Forum: all for ages 3-12<\/span>
                • \u201cEvery Day is a Holiday!\u201d, 9:00-12:00 each day; $32\/day<\/span><\/li>
                • \u201cSummer Olympics\u201d, 1:00-4:00 each day, $32\/day<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li>
                • MSU 4-H Children\u2019s Garden Camp Monet<\/span><\/span><\/a> - July 30 - Aug 1<\/span>
                  • $85, Ages 7 and up<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li>
                  • TinkrLabs<\/span><\/a><\/span> Camps - enroll for all 5 days of the week of the Forum<\/span>
                    • Animal Adventure<\/span><\/a><\/span>, 9am-12pm, Grades K-5<\/span><\/li>
                    • \u201cLet\u2019s Get Messy\u201d<\/span><\/span><\/a>, 1-4pm each day; Grades K-5, cost varies, but close to $300<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li>
                    • MSU <\/span>Ice Hockey<\/span><\/span><\/a> Sports Camp during the week of the Forum<\/span><\/li>
                    • Reach Studio Art Summer Camp<\/a><\/span><\/li><\/ul>


                      If you have questions about any of this information, please reach out to us at <\/span>                      forum@diglib.org<\/span><\/span><\/a>.<\/span><\/p>","_id":"d9f9bbc"},{"tab_title":"Conference Spaces","tab_content":"

                      Floor Plans and Virtual Tours<\/span><\/h4>

                      View the floor plans and virtual tours of the conference venues below. Learn more about the venues <\/span>on the Conference Venues and Hotels page<\/span>.<\/span><\/a> While onsite, attendees may utilize the MSU Guide App<\/a><\/span> as a way to help navigate.<\/p>

                      MSU Main Library\u00a0<\/b><\/p>

                      Floor Plans<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/p>

                      Virtual Tour<\/span><\/a><\/span> - If these virtual tours are inaccessible to you, please contact <\/span>accessibility@lib.msu.edu<\/span><\/span><\/a> to request an in-person tour or a written floor plan description.<\/span><\/p>

                      Wells Hall<\/b><\/p>

                      Annotated Floor Plan<\/a><\/span><\/p>

                      Virtual Tour<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/p>

                      MSU Broad Art Museum\u00a0<\/b><\/p>

                      Virtual Tour<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/p>

                      If you have questions about access or wish to request special accommodations, please contact Dana Steiner, Visitor Services Coordinator, at <\/span>steine58@msu.edu<\/span><\/span><\/a> or (517) 884-4813.<\/span><\/p>


                      Accessing the Conference Spaces<\/span><\/h4>

                      MSU Main Library<\/b><\/p>

                      The Library has a North entrance (West Circle Dr.) if you\u2019re coming from Grand River Ave. and a South (back) entrance (Red Cedar Rd.) if you\u2019re coming from Owen Halls or Wells Hall.<\/span><\/p>

                      The North entrance<\/a><\/span><\/strong> is not wheelchair accessible<\/strong>. There are 3 (stairs) for the North entrance, two of them lead to the north door and one leads to the east door. These doors are not locked during off-hours to allow library patrons to collect borrowed library material from the self-serve lockers. Automatic\/power assisted door opener is available for the east doors entrance.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

                      The short hallway after the entrance door leads visitors to the inside doors of the main building. These inside doors are locked during off-hours. There are security gates present inside the building.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

                      The South entrance<\/a><\/span><\/strong> is wheelchair accessible<\/strong> via an all access ramp and has automatic\/power assisted door opener for both the outside entrance doors and inside doors. Both doors are locked during off-hours. There are security gates present inside the building.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

                      All elevators have Braille and tactile numbering and lettering both outside and inside each elevator.<\/span><\/p>

                      Wells Hall<\/b><\/p>

                      Entrance from the Red Cedar Rd.<\/span><\/span><\/a><\/p>

                      Exit from the library back door and walk across the bridge. Turn left on the sidewalk (either the one along the river or along the street) and walk toward the building. The entrance is wheelchair accessible, but it has no Automatic\/power assisted door opener.<\/span><\/p>

                      You'll arrive in the A-wing of the building. Keep walking through the hallway until almost reaching the opposite entrance doors, turn right using the ramp walkway, and keep going until you reach the B119 room. We'll have DLF signage in front of the room.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

                      Entrance from the quad<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/p>

                      Walk from the library back door, turn left before the bridge and walk along the river until you get to the second bridge. Cross the bridge and walk toward the building. Keep walking past the bicycle parking spots. The closest entrance to the B119 room is the double doors with the wheelchair signage next to the seating area (see picture linked above). Turn right after you enter the building to get to the B119 room.<\/span><\/p>

                      MSU Broad Art Museum<\/b><\/p>

                      The main entrance of the museum is wheelchair accessible via an all-access ramp and has an automated power assisted door.<\/span><\/p>

                      Mobility\u00a0<\/b><\/p>

                      MSU Libraries is fully wheelchair-accessible, however it does not have wheelchairs available for borrowing. The Library has an Amigo motorized cart to help patrons move throughout the building and shopping carts that conference attendees can borrow while in the building. When you register, please let us know if there are any mobility assistance needs you may have during the Forum, and we\u2019ll be in contact to help address them as well as we can. If you have any questions, please email us at <\/span>forum@diglib.org<\/span><\/span><\/a>.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>


                      Meeting Rooms<\/span><\/h4>

                      MSU Main Library<\/b><\/p>

                      • All library classrooms have dimmable lighting.\u00a0<\/span><\/li>
                      • Temperature in classrooms can be adjusted by asking CLIR staff.<\/span><\/li>
                      • Not all rooms in the library are equipped with curtains or window coverings.\u00a0<\/span><\/li><\/ul>

                        Wells Hall<\/b><\/p>

                        The space we\u2019ll be using in Wells is a large lecture hall space with auditorium seating and no windows.<\/span><\/p>

                        MSU Broad Art Museum<\/b><\/p>

                        No sessions will take place at the Museum, only the opening reception.<\/span><\/p>

                        Restrooms<\/span><\/h4>

                        MSU Main Library<\/b><\/p>

                        • 1st floor restrooms:<\/span>
                          • Single-gender<\/span><\/li>
                          • One ADA stall in each restroom<\/span><\/li>
                          • Baby changing station is available in both restrooms<\/span><\/li>
                          • Equipped with automatic \/ power-assisted doors<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li>
                          • 2nd floor restrooms, West Wing:\u00a0<\/span>
                            • All-gender and single-gender restrooms available<\/span><\/li>
                            • One ADA stall in single-gender restroom<\/span><\/li>
                            • No automatic \/ power-assisted doors<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li>
                            • 3rd floor restrooms, West Wing:\u00a0<\/span>
                              • All-gender and single-gender restrooms available<\/span><\/li>
                              • One ADA stall in single-gender restroom\u00a0<\/span><\/li>
                              • No automatic \/ power-assisted doors<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li>
                              • 4th floor restrooms, West Wing, nearest conference meeting rooms:<\/span>
                                • Single-gender<\/span><\/li>
                                • No ADA stall in these restrooms<\/span><\/li>
                                • No automatic \/ power-assisted doors<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li>
                                • 4th floor restrooms, West Wing, near Music Library:<\/span>
                                  • All-gender and single-gender restrooms available\u00a0<\/span><\/li>
                                  • One ADA stall in each restroom. The all-gender restroom has grab bars for right transfer, the women's restroom has grab bars for left transfer.<\/span><\/li>
                                  • No automatic \/ power-assisted doors<\/span><\/li><\/ul><\/li><\/ul>

                                    Wells Hall<\/b><\/p>

                                    A single use restroom is available on each floor of the Wells B-wing. It is located around the building from B119. The single-use restroom is also ADA compliant.<\/span><\/p>

                                    MSU Broad Art Museum<\/b><\/p>

                                    Single-gender restrooms are available on the 1st floor next to the Museum Shop area. There are two ADA stalls in the women\u2019s restroom.<\/span><\/p>

                                    Outdoor Space<\/span><\/h4>

                                    The MSU campus has copious outdoor space where attendees can take a break and get some fresh air. There are a number of outdoor move-able chairs and a large lawn in front of Wells Hall as well as along the river in between the Main Library building and Wells Hall.<\/span><\/p>

                                    Quiet Room\u00a0<\/span><\/h4>

                                    The Quiet Room is intended to provide a quiet, calm space where conference attendees can spend time away from noise, lights, and other stimuli of conference spaces. It is not available for conversations or meetings. The Quiet Room will be located in W207, the CTLI Instruction Room, near the Microprint \/ Microform Guides on the 2nd floor. All-gender and single-gender restrooms are available near the Quiet Room.<\/span><\/p>

                                    Smoking and Smoke-Free Areas<\/span><\/h4>

                                    The MSU campus is entirely smoke-free. If you\u2019d like to know more about fragrance at the conference, see the section below, Fragrance at the Forum.<\/span><\/p>

                                    Air Circulation and Filtration<\/span><\/h4>

                                    MSU has a mixture of MERV 11 and MERV 13 filters in the air handling units across campus. The Library air handling runs 24\/7. Wells Hall B119 air circulation runs based on room usage.<\/span><\/p>","_id":"06ff8b6"},{"tab_title":"Photography","tab_content":"

                                    When you register for our event, you will have the option to tell us whether or not you would like to be photographed. We ask our attendees to not photograph, video, or audio record anyone without their express permission. Attendees will have differentiated badge lanyards showing their preference for photography.<\/span><\/p>

                                    \u00a0<\/p>

                                    Black lanyards: Photographs are okay<\/span><\/p>

                                    Yellow lanyards: Please don\u2019t take my photograph<\/span><\/p>","_id":"077ff50"},{"tab_title":"Accessibility","tab_content":"

                                    Accessibility at MSU Libraries<\/span><\/h4>

                                    Lots of information about accessibility at MSU Libraries can be found here.<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/p>

                                    Accessible Presentations<\/span><\/h4>

                                    We ask that all presenters review our <\/span>Creating Accessible Presentations webinar<\/span><\/a> and submit their presentations in our conference repository on Open Science Framework (OSF). We recommend that presenters submit their presentations before or during the conference for attendees to access them. OSF links are organized by conference and are available on the <\/span>shared notes and slides page<\/span><\/a>.<\/span><\/p>

                                    Listening Systems<\/span><\/h4>

                                    Library classrooms are not equipped with an in-room listening system. <\/span>An assistive listening device is available for events or meetings taking place in the Library Green Room (4th floor). <\/span>If you\u2019d like to request accommodations or if you have questions, please let us know at <\/span>forum@diglib.org<\/span><\/a>.<\/span><\/p>

                                    Microphones<\/span><\/h4>

                                    Microphones will be used for all speakers during the opening and closing plenary sessions. All breakout rooms in the library have mics at the podiums and in some cases have lavalier and\/or handheld mics as well. Speakers will be encouraged to repeat attendee questions into a microphone if an audience microphone is not available.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

                                    Livestreaming and Recording<\/span><\/h4>

                                    We plan to livestream the opening and closing plenaries for the DLF Forum as well as provide partial or full recordings on our Featured Speakers page.<\/span><\/p>

                                    Hotel Accommodations<\/span><\/h4>

                                    If you require an ADA compliant or accessible hotel room, please let your hotel know directly during your room reservation process. This includes needs like an accessible restroom, a bathtub, room located close to elevators, a fragrance-free room, etc.<\/span><\/p>

                                    Fragrance at the Forum<\/span><\/h4>

                                    MSU Main Library<\/b><\/p>

                                    The Library does not use scent diffusers in any areas. Cleaning products do not have a fragrance, but may have a cleaning product smell which may linger. Additionally, library staff are expected to avoid wearing fragrances that could potentially become a distraction to their patrons.<\/span><\/p>

                                    For the comfort and safety of those with chemical sensitivities, the DLF Forum is a fragrance-free event. Please refrain from wearing products such as perfumes\/colognes, scented lotions, and clothing with strong detergent scents while attending. Thank you for your consideration for all members of our community.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

                                    Wells Hall<\/b><\/p>

                                    Wells Hall also does not use scent diffusers, nor do any other campus locations (per MSU Facilities). Like in the Libraries, cleaning products do not have a fragrance, but may have a cleaning product smell which may linger. <\/span><\/p>

                                    MSU Broad Art Museum<\/b><\/p>

                                    The planning team is working to determine what fragrances, if any, are utilized at the Museum.<\/span><\/p>


                                    More information on being fragrance-free can be found here:<\/span><\/p>

                                    • Accessible Spaces: A Fragrance-Free Toolkit<\/span><\/span><\/a><\/li>
                                    • Think Before You Stink<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/li><\/ul>","_id":"4e716ee"},{"tab_title":"Dining","tab_content":"

                                      Local Dining Options<\/b><\/p>

                                      Our Community Committee has developed a guide to local dining and entertainment options. <\/span>Find it on our Local Guide page.<\/span><\/a><\/span><\/p>

                                      Dietary Requirements at Our Events<\/b><\/p>

                                      Attendees will receive two meal tickets for MSU campus dining facilities for lunch on Tuesday and Wednesday. These facilities strive to meet all dietary requirements. DLF will also provide coffee and light refreshments at other times throughout the conference and will work to ensure everything is well-labeled. Please let us know your dietary requirements when you register, and contact us at <\/span>forum@diglib.org<\/span><\/a> for more detailed information.<\/span><\/p>

                                      Reception<\/b><\/p>

                                      With registration to the DLF Forum, we will provide one complimentary beverage ticket (included in your welcome packet) to be redeemed at the Monday night opening reception. We will offer creative spirit-free cocktails, soft drinks, and alcoholic beverages.<\/span><\/p>","_id":"3417164"},{"tab_title":"Other Resources","tab_content":"

                                      • Community Mental Health for Central Michigan<\/span><\/a> - If you or someone you know is in crisis and needs immediate assistance, call their Crisis Hotline at 1-800-317-0708; 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.<\/span><\/li>
                                      • DLF\u2019s emergency\/Code of Conduct number at (732) 737-7328 (732-RESPECT). This number will be continuously monitored by CLIR\/DLF staff during our in-person events between the hours of 7am and 9pm in the time zone of the Resources for Attendees

[elementor-element k="69ea058a3f60854a6b4931f7ab9ec816" data=""]

Common questions answered

Welcome to the Guide

[elementor-element k="69ea058a3f60854a6b4931f7ab9ec816" data=""]
Code of Conduct

Please review our DLF Code of Conduct prior to joining us at the Forum. On site, DLF staff will be identifiable by their name badges and white lanyards.

For First-Time Attendees

We hope our first-time attendees will feel empowered and comfortable when they attend our events. The DLF Community Committee typically plans social and newcomers’ events – check the Wellness and Activities page for more information. 

Before the events:

  • When you register, consider signing up for the DLF mentorship program. 
  • We encourage you to select or enter your pronouns to appear on your conference badge when you register and create your user account on our conference management system. This is an entirely optional field, and we welcome everyone to make a selection.
  • There’s no strict dress code at the Forum, but attendees tend to gravitate towards business casual attire. See photos from last year for a better idea. Additionally, meeting rooms can be chilly, so consider keeping a sweater or jacket on hand just in case.


During the events:

  • All sessions at the Forum are open to anyone—Working Group meetings (aka DLF Working Sessions) included. Please feel free to join these whether you’re interested in joining group activities or just learning more about them.
  • We are completely aware of how hard conferencing can be, and want you to have a good experience. Know it’s ok to leave a session if it’s not what you were expecting, or to miss one entirely because you’re otherwise occupied or just need a break. There will be a designated Quiet Room onsite for anyone who wants to recharge or get some work done.
  • Every session has a shared notes doc if you want to catch up on something you missed (or contribute for others), and presenters will be encouraged to upload slides to DLF’s OSF repository. Links are available on the shared notes and slides page.
  • Have a question for organizers during the events? Let us know by stopping by the registration desk, stopping anyone with a white lanyard (which indicates staff), or emailing us at forum@diglib.org.
Active Bystander Orientation

Have you ever witnessed bullying, harassment, or an uncomfortable encounter in a professional context and wished you knew how to intervene? It can be challenging to know what to say or do on the spot. The DLF Code of Conduct invites participants to be Active Bystanders, but what does that really mean?

DLF’s Committee for Equity and Inclusion hosted an Active Bystander Orientation on October 24, 2023, ahead of the 2023 DLF Forum and affiliated events. This presentation provides an introduction to bystander intervention and an overview of strategies.

View the recording here.

Slides are here.

Suggested readings and resources are here.

Transportation - Getting to East Lansing

The MSU campus is a 15-minute drive from Capital Regional International Airport. Taxicab service costs approximately $15. 

It is a 75-minute (90 mile) drive from Detroit Metro Airport. The Michigan Flyer Airport Shuttle offers bus transportation to East Lansing for approximately $30. Buses run several times a day, and travel takes approximately two hours. 

East Lansing is also accessible from the smaller Gerald R. Ford International Airport in Grand Rapids. It’s a 60-minute (65 mile) drive between the two.

The Capital Area Multimodal Gateway on campus houses the Amtrak Blue Water train stop as well as Greyhound and Indian Trails bus services.

Local CATA (Capital Area Transportation Authority) bus routes stop at the station, and the facility also offers taxicab and bike-sharing services.

MSU campus transportation information is also available, as is information about campus safety.


Parking at MSU

There are pay-by-plate lots or metered spaces around campus. Parking rates are $2 per hour. Check for more parking information at MSU Police Parking Office Page and find visitor parking here. Additionally, information about complimentary parking at MSU is available here. Accessible parking spaces are available to vehicles with the appropriate state-issued disability parking placard at any time.

MSU Main Library

Accessible parking for the library is located on the east side of the Main Library, and at the South (back) entrance. MSU Museum across the library also has an accessibility parking spot. 

Wells Hall

Accessible parking spots for Wells Hall are located on Red Cedar Rd., the east side of Wells. 

MSU Broad Art Museum

The nearest designated accessible parking spaces can be found directly south of the museum in Lot 8 (next to the Student Services building). Additional accessible parking areas can be found in the Grand River parking structure (Ramp 6), as well as north of Grand River Avenue in the City of East Lansing surface lots.

Health Protocols

While CLIR/DLF will not be issuing event-specific health protocol announcements in 2024, we maintain and reinforce the following:

  • Masking will be recommended but not required at the DLF Forum at Michigan State University.
  • Our events will be mask-friendly, meaning anyone who wants to wear a mask will be welcome to do so, no questions asked. 
  • CLIR will have masks, tests, and sanitizer available free of charge at the registration desk for anyone who needs them.
  • Any harassment related to masking will be a violation of our Code of Conduct and may be reported and consequences enforced in the same way as any other CoC violation.
  • CLIR will communicate promptly and transparently to all attendees if we learn of a positive test at the Forum. 
  • CLIR will communicate these expectations openly and regularly to all prospective and registered attendees in the weeks leading up to the events.

If you have questions, please send us an email at forum@diglib.org. 

Emergency and Local Care Information

Should an emergency or otherwise unexpected serious disruption occur, please phone emergency services at 911 immediately. 

DLF staff (who will be clearly designated for the duration of the Forum with name badges and white lanyards) will be onsite to assist by contacting hotel/venue security or local law enforcement, providing escorts, or otherwise helping address the situation in the swiftest, most calm and organized way possible. 

You can also reach CLIR/DLF staff at our emergency/Code of Conduct number at (732) 737-7328 (732-RESPECT) between 7am and 9pm local time. Outside of those hours, please contact the hotel or dial 911 for any after-hours emergencies.

 

Hospitals near Michigan State University

  • McLaren Greater Lansing Hospital Emergency Room (3.7 miles away / 11 minute drive) – 2900 Collins Rd., Lansing, 48910. Phone: 517-975-7500.
  • E.W. Sparrow Hospital Emergency Room (3.7 miles away / 11 minute drive) – 1215 E. Michigan Ave., Lansing, 48912. Phone: 877-727-7691.


Urgent care centers near Michigan State University

Please call or visit their websites to learn more about their limited hours. 

  • Sparrow Urgent Care (2 miles away / 7 minute drive) – 2682 E. Grand River Ave., East Lansing, 48823. Phone: 517-333-6562
  • Lansing Urgent Care – Frandor (2.5 mile away / 9 minute drive) – 505 N. Clippert St., Lansing, 48912. Phone: 517-999-2273
For Families

Nursing Room

We will provide a nursing room onsite for those who prefer a quiet, private place to breastfeed their baby or pump. However, please feed your baby whenever and wherever you like. We strive to be a friendly environment for families.

Please ask for the key to the nursing room at the conference registration desk. This room is accessible to one family at a time and is located in a private classroom room away from the conference spaces. The room has chairs and a table and is across the hallway from a kitchen and a bathroom.

Childcare and Summer Camp Options

While we are not able to provide onsite childcare at the DLF Forum this year, the planning team has compiled a list of resources that may help. Note that many childcare places near campus do not allow for drop ins, including Spartan Child Development Center and People’s Church Preschool.

  • Bailey Preschool
    • $60-75 daily on a space-available basis. 
    • Reservations need to be made at least two weeks in advance
  • Hannah Community Center School-age summer camps
  • Launch Trampoline Park: $35 day pass
  • YMCA camps
  • GymKind Gymnastics Camps (in Meridian Mall in Okemos). Options during during the week of the Forum: all for ages 3-12
    • “Every Day is a Holiday!”, 9:00-12:00 each day; $32/day
    • “Summer Olympics”, 1:00-4:00 each day, $32/day
  • MSU 4-H Children’s Garden Camp Monet – July 30 – Aug 1
    • $85, Ages 7 and up
  • TinkrLabs Camps – enroll for all 5 days of the week of the Forum
    • Animal Adventure, 9am-12pm, Grades K-5
    • “Let’s Get Messy”, 1-4pm each day; Grades K-5, cost varies, but close to $300
  • MSU Ice Hockey Sports Camp during the week of the Forum
  • Reach Studio Art Summer Camp


If you have questions about any of this information, please reach out to us at forum@diglib.org.

Conference Spaces

Floor Plans and Virtual Tours

View the floor plans and virtual tours of the conference venues below. Learn more about the venues on the Conference Venues and Hotels page. While onsite, attendees may utilize the MSU Guide App as a way to help navigate.

MSU Main Library 

Floor Plans

Virtual Tour – If these virtual tours are inaccessible to you, please contact accessibility@lib.msu.edu to request an in-person tour or a written floor plan description.

Wells Hall

Annotated Floor Plan

Virtual Tour

MSU Broad Art Museum 

Virtual Tour

If you have questions about access or wish to request special accommodations, please contact Dana Steiner, Visitor Services Coordinator, at steine58@msu.edu or (517) 884-4813.


Accessing the Conference Spaces

MSU Main Library

The Library has a North entrance (West Circle Dr.) if you’re coming from Grand River Ave. and a South (back) entrance (Red Cedar Rd.) if you’re coming from Owen Halls or Wells Hall.

The North entrance is not wheelchair accessible. There are 3 (stairs) for the North entrance, two of them lead to the north door and one leads to the east door. These doors are not locked during off-hours to allow library patrons to collect borrowed library material from the self-serve lockers. Automatic/power assisted door opener is available for the east doors entrance. 

The short hallway after the entrance door leads visitors to the inside doors of the main building. These inside doors are locked during off-hours. There are security gates present inside the building. 

The South entrance is wheelchair accessible via an all access ramp and has automatic/power assisted door opener for both the outside entrance doors and inside doors. Both doors are locked during off-hours. There are security gates present inside the building. 

All elevators have Braille and tactile numbering and lettering both outside and inside each elevator.

Wells Hall

Entrance from the Red Cedar Rd.

Exit from the library back door and walk across the bridge. Turn left on the sidewalk (either the one along the river or along the street) and walk toward the building. The entrance is wheelchair accessible, but it has no Automatic/power assisted door opener.

You’ll arrive in the A-wing of the building. Keep walking through the hallway until almost reaching the opposite entrance doors, turn right using the ramp walkway, and keep going until you reach the B119 room. We’ll have DLF signage in front of the room. 

Entrance from the quad

Walk from the library back door, turn left before the bridge and walk along the river until you get to the second bridge. Cross the bridge and walk toward the building. Keep walking past the bicycle parking spots. The closest entrance to the B119 room is the double doors with the wheelchair signage next to the seating area (see picture linked above). Turn right after you enter the building to get to the B119 room.

MSU Broad Art Museum

The main entrance of the museum is wheelchair accessible via an all-access ramp and has an automated power assisted door.

Mobility 

MSU Libraries is fully wheelchair-accessible, however it does not have wheelchairs available for borrowing. The Library has an Amigo motorized cart to help patrons move throughout the building and shopping carts that conference attendees can borrow while in the building. When you register, please let us know if there are any mobility assistance needs you may have during the Forum, and we’ll be in contact to help address them as well as we can. If you have any questions, please email us at forum@diglib.org. 


Meeting Rooms

MSU Main Library

  • All library classrooms have dimmable lighting. 
  • Temperature in classrooms can be adjusted by asking CLIR staff.
  • Not all rooms in the library are equipped with curtains or window coverings. 

Wells Hall

The space we’ll be using in Wells is a large lecture hall space with auditorium seating and no windows.

MSU Broad Art Museum

No sessions will take place at the Museum, only the opening reception.

Restrooms

MSU Main Library

  • 1st floor restrooms:
    • Single-gender
    • One ADA stall in each restroom
    • Baby changing station is available in both restrooms
    • Equipped with automatic / power-assisted doors
  • 2nd floor restrooms, West Wing: 
    • All-gender and single-gender restrooms available
    • One ADA stall in single-gender restroom
    • No automatic / power-assisted doors
  • 3rd floor restrooms, West Wing: 
    • All-gender and single-gender restrooms available
    • One ADA stall in single-gender restroom 
    • No automatic / power-assisted doors
  • 4th floor restrooms, West Wing, nearest conference meeting rooms:
    • Single-gender
    • No ADA stall in these restrooms
    • No automatic / power-assisted doors
  • 4th floor restrooms, West Wing, near Music Library:
    • All-gender and single-gender restrooms available 
    • One ADA stall in each restroom. The all-gender restroom has grab bars for right transfer, the women’s restroom has grab bars for left transfer.
    • No automatic / power-assisted doors

Wells Hall

A single use restroom is available on each floor of the Wells B-wing. It is located around the building from B119. The single-use restroom is also ADA compliant.

MSU Broad Art Museum

Single-gender restrooms are available on the 1st floor next to the Museum Shop area. There are two ADA stalls in the women’s restroom.

Outdoor Space

The MSU campus has copious outdoor space where attendees can take a break and get some fresh air. There are a number of outdoor move-able chairs and a large lawn in front of Wells Hall as well as along the river in between the Main Library building and Wells Hall.

Quiet Room 

The Quiet Room is intended to provide a quiet, calm space where conference attendees can spend time away from noise, lights, and other stimuli of conference spaces. It is not available for conversations or meetings. The Quiet Room will be located in W207, the CTLI Instruction Room, near the Microprint / Microform Guides on the 2nd floor. All-gender and single-gender restrooms are available near the Quiet Room.

Smoking and Smoke-Free Areas

The MSU campus is entirely smoke-free. If you’d like to know more about fragrance at the conference, see the section below, Fragrance at the Forum.

Air Circulation and Filtration

MSU has a mixture of MERV 11 and MERV 13 filters in the air handling units across campus. The Library air handling runs 24/7. Wells Hall B119 air circulation runs based on room usage.

Photography

When you register for our event, you will have the option to tell us whether or not you would like to be photographed. We ask our attendees to not photograph, video, or audio record anyone without their express permission. Attendees will have differentiated badge lanyards showing their preference for photography.

 

Black lanyards: Photographs are okay

Yellow lanyards: Please don’t take my photograph

Accessibility

Accessibility at MSU Libraries

Lots of information about accessibility at MSU Libraries can be found here.

Accessible Presentations

We ask that all presenters review our Creating Accessible Presentations webinar and submit their presentations in our conference repository on Open Science Framework (OSF). We recommend that presenters submit their presentations before or during the conference for attendees to access them. OSF links are organized by conference and are available on the shared notes and slides page.

Listening Systems

Library classrooms are not equipped with an in-room listening system. An assistive listening device is available for events or meetings taking place in the Library Green Room (4th floor). If you’d like to request accommodations or if you have questions, please let us know at forum@diglib.org.

Microphones

Microphones will be used for all speakers during the opening and closing plenary sessions. All breakout rooms in the library have mics at the podiums and in some cases have lavalier and/or handheld mics as well. Speakers will be encouraged to repeat attendee questions into a microphone if an audience microphone is not available. 

Livestreaming and Recording

We plan to livestream the opening and closing plenaries for the DLF Forum as well as provide partial or full recordings on our Featured Speakers page.

Hotel Accommodations

If you require an ADA compliant or accessible hotel room, please let your hotel know directly during your room reservation process. This includes needs like an accessible restroom, a bathtub, room located close to elevators, a fragrance-free room, etc.

Fragrance at the Forum

MSU Main Library

The Library does not use scent diffusers in any areas. Cleaning products do not have a fragrance, but may have a cleaning product smell which may linger. Additionally, library staff are expected to avoid wearing fragrances that could potentially become a distraction to their patrons.

For the comfort and safety of those with chemical sensitivities, the DLF Forum is a fragrance-free event. Please refrain from wearing products such as perfumes/colognes, scented lotions, and clothing with strong detergent scents while attending. Thank you for your consideration for all members of our community. 

Wells Hall

Wells Hall also does not use scent diffusers, nor do any other campus locations (per MSU Facilities). Like in the Libraries, cleaning products do not have a fragrance, but may have a cleaning product smell which may linger.

MSU Broad Art Museum

The planning team is working to determine what fragrances, if any, are utilized at the Museum.


More information on being fragrance-free can be found here:

  • Accessible Spaces: A Fragrance-Free Toolkit
  • Think Before You Stink
Dining

Local Dining Options

Our Community Committee has developed a guide to local dining and entertainment options. Find it on our Local Guide page.

Dietary Requirements at Our Events

Attendees will receive two meal tickets for MSU campus dining facilities for lunch on Tuesday and Wednesday. These facilities strive to meet all dietary requirements. DLF will also provide coffee and light refreshments at other times throughout the conference and will work to ensure everything is well-labeled. Please let us know your dietary requirements when you register, and contact us at forum@diglib.org for more detailed information.

Reception

With registration to the DLF Forum, we will provide one complimentary beverage ticket (included in your welcome packet) to be redeemed at the Monday night opening reception. We will offer creative spirit-free cocktails, soft drinks, and alcoholic beverages.

Other Resources
  • Community Mental Health for Central Michigan – If you or someone you know is in crisis and needs immediate assistance, call their Crisis Hotline at 1-800-317-0708; 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
  • DLF’s emergency/Code of Conduct number at (732) 737-7328 (732-RESPECT). This number will be continuously monitored by CLIR/DLF staff during our in-person events between the hours of 7am and 9pm in the time zone of the events.

Is something missing from this list?

Welcome to the Local Guide for East Lansing, Michigan, the city where the in-person DLF Forum is happening! Big thank you to the 2024 DLF Forum Community Committee for creating this guide. Keep in mind this guide is not exhaustive and there might be unforeseen issues such as construction, so please be sure to check the navigation before heading out to any of these suggestions.

Information about East Lansing

Use these resources to follow local East Lansing / Lansing / MSU news before and during your visit.

  • Lansing State Journal
  • State News – student newspaper
  • City Pulse – weekly alternative newspaper


East Lansing Info – local news reporting

East Lansing History and Context

Learn about East Lansing before arriving at the Forum.

  • East Lansing Centennial 1907-2007 (MSU Archives online exhibit)
  • Greater Lansing history timeline
  • African American History Trail


Resource for supporting LGBTQ+-owned businesses (State News, 2022)

Where to Eat

Campus/Surrounding East Lansing East Lansing/Okemos Lansing Campus/Surrounding East Lansing

These spots are less than 1 mile from campus.

  • Aloha Cookin’: Hawaiian food near campus (closed Mondays and Tuesdays)
  • BAPS Home Style Korean BBQ: $20-30 per person, A KBBQ restaurant that has an assortment of Korean dishes. Their lunch specials are a deal less than $15 for a filling meal.
  • Campus dining halls: Brody (flagship), Akers, Case Hall South Pointe have the most variety. Compare daily menus, most are all-you-care-to-eat. Venues are accessible via elevator or on a ground-level floor, menus provide options for vegetarian, gluten-free, Kosher, Halal and other dietary needs. Public dining rates: Breakfast: $9 plus tax; Lunch or Dinner: $13 plus tax; Children (ages 2-9 years): $6.75 plus tax
  • Charlie Kang’s: $10-20 per person, Chinese and Korean cuisine with a wide range of flavors, near campus.
  • Crossroads Food Court at the International Center: $1-20 per person. A food court featuring Subway, Panda Express, Woody’s Oasis Mediterranean Deli, and the Roost
  • El Azteco: $10-20 per person, casual Mexican food with a rooftop dining area in business since 1976.
  • For Crepe Sake: $10-20 per person, near campus this breakfast and lunch spot has evening service Thursday to Saturday. Their menu has sweet and savory crepes, Belgian waffles, fruit smoothies and more.
  • Playa Bowls: $10-20 per person. A health food restaurant chain.
  • Sapporo Ramen & Noodle Bar: $10-20 per person, cozy ramen bar offering vegetarian options.
  • State Room (Kellogg Center): $30-50 per person. High-end dining. They have all-you-can-eat buffets M-F for $14 (plus tax) and a la carte dinner.
East Lansing/Okemos
  • Black-owned restaurants (curated list by Lansing Foodies)
  • Coral Gables: $10-20 per person, originally built in the 1920s as a roadhouse is now a family restaurant with an assortment of Americana food and private meeting rooms.
  • Cottage Inn: $10-20 per person. A midwestern chain serving deep-dish and thin-crust pizza, salads, etc.
  • Bell’s Greek Pizza: $1-10 per person, this pizza joint has been in East Lansing since 1967. The menu has pizza, pasta and other Mediterranean food.
  • Everyday Authentic Chinese Cuisine: $20-30 per person, serves Cantonese style food and some American Chinese favorites.
  • Georgio’s Pizza: $1-10 per person, small chain pizzeria offering unique pizza styles.
  • Grand Traverse Pie Company
  • Korea House Restaurant
  • Pizza House: $10-20 per person. A family-owned local pizza chain with locations in East Lansing and Ann Arbor for Chicago-style pizza.
  • Sindhu Indian Cuisine: $10-20 per person, North and South Indian food, family run with many vegetarian options. They have buffets on Sundays
  • Sree Saffron: $10-20 per person, Indian cuisine (near Sindhu in the Hannah Plaza)
  • Thai Princess (Okemos): $20-30 per person, variety of Thai specialties. A local favorite for Thai food.
  • Tabooli Mediterranean
  • Woody’s Oasis: $10-20 per person, casual Mediterranean food with many options, been in East Lansing for over 35
Lansing

Frandor / Eastside

  • Altu’s Ethiopian Cuisine & Bar: $10-20 per person, locally owned informal eatery with a variety of meat and vegetarian Ethiopian dishes.
  • Jersey Giant Subs: Up to $10 per person, an East Lansing family-owned sub restaurant since 1979. Offers a wide variety of sub sandwiches. Many locations around the area.
  • People’s Kitchen: $20-30 per person, comfort foods & craft cocktails served amid colorful industrial decor, plus weekend brunch.
  • Ruckus Ramen: $10-20 per person, unique take on East Asian cuisine located within The Avenue bar on the Eastside of Lansing.
  • Soup Spoon Cafe: $10-20 per person, full service restaurant and bar known for their ‘scratch’ kitchen and craft cocktails.


Downtown

  • EnVie: $20-30 per person, a bistro in the heart of Lansing’s downtown area with a rotating menu. Open Tuesday through Saturday for dinner only.
  • Golden Harvest: $10-20 per person, legendary grungy breakfast joint in Lansing. Cash only.
  • Lansing Shuffle: Food hall with ~7 different cuisines represented, on the Grand River in downtown Lansing


Old Town

  • Meat Southern BBQ and Carnivore Cuisine: $10-20 per person, local BBQ joint with kitschy interior. There can be a wait.
  • The Cosmos: $10-20 per person. Wood-fired pizza with a connected full bar, Zoobie’s Old Town Tavern, in Lansing’s Old Town neighborhood.


Westside Lansing

  • Horrocks Farm Market: $10-20 per person, has gelato, beer, wine bar, sushi and other pre-made food. Located within Lansing’s quintessential farm market. Started in 1959 as a road-side fruit stand, this market has grown and evolved over the years. Has a beer garden nestled in their outdoor plant market which often hosts local events.
  • Ohana Sushi: $30-40 per person, all-you-can-eat sushi made with fresh and, when possible, local ingredients.

Local Guide Map

Where to Drink

Coffee Bars and Breweries Coffee

Find these great coffee spots in downtown East Lansing.

  • Foster Coffee Company: a Michigan-based coffee shop is housed within a modern/industrial design space.
  • Haraz Coffee House: Yemeni coffee shop and bakery with locations across the country.
  • Koala Tea & Coffee: Milk tea and bubble tea with baked goods. Their Okemos location has a robot that will deliver your food to you.
  • Moka & Co.: Yemeni specialty coffee shop with incredible baked goods.
  • Strange Matter: Woman-owned local coffee bar and bakery that is very active in the community. There are three locations in the area, with the closest being in MSU’s Union building. Known for their donuts and pastries, their vegan gluten-free donuts are beloved.
Bars and Breweries
  • Beggar’s Banquet: $$, local American food restaurant and pub founded in 1973
  • Crunchy’s Burgers and Beers: $10-20 per person. Local American food restaurant and pub founded in 1982. Home to one of the area’s best burgers and its specialty “bucket of beer”.
  • Hopcat: $10-20 per person. A trendy Michigan-based chain bar
  • Jolly Pumpkin: $10-20 per person. Known for their sour beer. Serves burgers, pizza, and other pub staples.
  • Peanut Barrel: $$, local American food restaurant and pub founded in 1973
  • The Avenue: Set in the heart of Lansing’s eastside neighborhood, The Ave is home to Ruckus Ramen, pinball, pool and live music. LGBTQ+ safe space with mocktail options.

Explore Lansing

Where to Visit What to Do Where to Visit

Broad Museum: Housed in a spectacular building designed by Pritzker Prize-winning “starchitect” Zaha Hadid, the MSU Broad Museum boasts collection strengths in Greek and Roman antiquities; Mesoamerican sculptures and vessels; North American and European sculpture, prints, photographs, and paintings; and works in a variety of media from different African, Asian, Latin American, and Middle Eastern cultures. These collections are showcased in the CORE (Center for Object Research and Engagement), which offers unique opportunities to view, reflect on, and investigate art objects spanning 5,000 years of human history. Hours 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM, Wednesday-Sunday; admission free with online registration, available here: https://broadmuseum.msu.edu/visit/getting-here/ 

Garden tour – botanical, children’s: The Beal Botanical Garden offers free tours open to the public. Established in 1873, the W. J. Beal Botanical Garden is the oldest, continuously operated university botanical garden in the United States and illuminates the interconnectedness between people, plants, and place. This living laboratory encourages learning and exploration of the natural world.

Dairy Store: ​​Enjoy ice cream and cheese at the MSU Dairy Store, open Tuesdays-Sundays from 12-8 p.m.

Capitol tour: The Michigan Capitol is open to visitors Monday through Friday. Guided tours are available between 9:00 and 4:00.

Old Town: Old town offers unique experiences through special events and eclectic shops.

Curious Book Shop: The thinking person’s visit to East Lansing wouldn’t be complete without a browse through the three floors of new and used titles at Curious! Check out their layout at http://www.curiousbooks.com/layout.html and make a special effort to get there if you’re into Oziana, rare sci-fi and fantasy, or vintage magazines. After all, you’ll need something to read on the plane home, right? Open Sunday 12 PM – 5 PM, Monday-Saturday 10 AM – 7 PM, and yes, they validate parking!

Potter Park Zoo: This AZA accredited zoo has been around since 1920 and sits on the Lansing River Trail. Known for its otter exhibit and conservation education, Potter Park Zoo is a beloved part of the community. 

Abrams Planetarium: Shows for the public are on Friday and Saturday nights and Sunday afternoons

Note that the MSU Museum will be closed for 18 months beginning in July.

What to Do

Bike tours (MSU Bikes and Renova Bikes): Enjoy the Lansing River trail which goes through MSU’s campus on a bicycle. A great way to explore the area as you follow the Red Cedar River and Grand River as it meanders through East Lansing and Lansing.

 

Lansing Lugnuts baseball game: Lansing’s very own minor league baseball team. The stadium has outfield lawn seats which but up against a kid’s play area, making baseball games fun for the whole family.

 

The Robin Theatre: Located in Lansing’s historical REO town, this local theatre/book store hosts something for everyone. The theatre is located within a 100-year old store front and provides an intimate environment for enjoying an eclectic array of performances, from film festivals to poetry readings.


Bands in Town: Find out about live music happenings in town. Includes local and touring musicians.

Wait, there's more

Navigating conferences can be a complex task. Drawing insights from feedback provided by previous participants and with the collaborative efforts of groups such as our Community Committee and Committee on Equity and Inclusion working group, we have developed resources to help orient folks as much as possible.

All Resources

The Local Guide

[elementor-element k="69ea058a3f60854a6b4931f7ab9ec816" data=""]

What You'll Find Here

Information about East Lansing

Local News
East Lansing History and Context
Local News

Use these resources to follow local East Lansing / Lansing / MSU news before and during your visit.

  • Lansing State Journal
  • State News – student newspaper
  • City Pulse – weekly alternative newspaper


East Lansing Info – local news reporting

East Lansing History and Context

Learn about East Lansing before arriving at the Forum.

  • East Lansing Centennial 1907-2007 (MSU Archives online exhibit)
  • Greater Lansing history timeline
  • African American History Trail


Resource for supporting LGBTQ+-owned businesses (State News, 2022)

Where to Eat

Campus/Surrounding East Lansing
East Lansing/Okemos
Lansing
Campus/Surrounding East Lansing

These spots are less than 1 mile from campus.

  • Aloha Cookin’: Hawaiian food near campus (closed Mondays and Tuesdays)
  • BAPS Home Style Korean BBQ: $20-30 per person, A KBBQ restaurant that has an assortment of Korean dishes. Their lunch specials are a deal less than $15 for a filling meal.
  • Campus dining halls: Brody (flagship), Akers, Case Hall South Pointe have the most variety. Compare daily menus, most are all-you-care-to-eat. Venues are accessible via elevator or on a ground-level floor, menus provide options for vegetarian, gluten-free, Kosher, Halal and other dietary needs. Public dining rates: Breakfast: $9 plus tax; Lunch or Dinner: $13 plus tax; Children (ages 2-9 years): $6.75 plus tax
  • Charlie Kang’s: $10-20 per person, Chinese and Korean cuisine with a wide range of flavors, near campus.
  • Crossroads Food Court at the International Center: $1-20 per person. A food court featuring Subway, Panda Express, Woody’s Oasis Mediterranean Deli, and the Roost
  • El Azteco: $10-20 per person, casual Mexican food with a rooftop dining area in business since 1976.
  • For Crepe Sake: $10-20 per person, near campus this breakfast and lunch spot has evening service Thursday to Saturday. Their menu has sweet and savory crepes, Belgian waffles, fruit smoothies and more.
  • Playa Bowls: $10-20 per person. A health food restaurant chain.
  • Sapporo Ramen & Noodle Bar: $10-20 per person, cozy ramen bar offering vegetarian options.
  • State Room (Kellogg Center): $30-50 per person. High-end dining. They have all-you-can-eat buffets M-F for $14 (plus tax) and a la carte dinner.
East Lansing/Okemos
  • Black-owned restaurants (curated list by Lansing Foodies)
  • Coral Gables: $10-20 per person, originally built in the 1920s as a roadhouse is now a family restaurant with an assortment of Americana food and private meeting rooms.
  • Cottage Inn: $10-20 per person. A midwestern chain serving deep-dish and thin-crust pizza, salads, etc.
  • Bell’s Greek Pizza: $1-10 per person, this pizza joint has been in East Lansing since 1967. The menu has pizza, pasta and other Mediterranean food.
  • Everyday Authentic Chinese Cuisine: $20-30 per person, serves Cantonese style food and some American Chinese favorites.
  • Georgio’s Pizza: $1-10 per person, small chain pizzeria offering unique pizza styles.
  • Grand Traverse Pie Company
  • Korea House Restaurant
  • Pizza House: $10-20 per person. A family-owned local pizza chain with locations in East Lansing and Ann Arbor for Chicago-style pizza.
  • Sindhu Indian Cuisine: $10-20 per person, North and South Indian food, family run with many vegetarian options. They have buffets on Sundays
  • Sree Saffron: $10-20 per person, Indian cuisine (near Sindhu in the Hannah Plaza)
  • Thai Princess (Okemos): $20-30 per person, variety of Thai specialties. A local favorite for Thai food.
  • Tabooli Mediterranean
  • Woody’s Oasis: $10-20 per person, casual Mediterranean food with many options, been in East Lansing for over 35
Lansing

Frandor / Eastside

  • Altu’s Ethiopian Cuisine & Bar: $10-20 per person, locally owned informal eatery with a variety of meat and vegetarian Ethiopian dishes.
  • Jersey Giant Subs: Up to $10 per person, an East Lansing family-owned sub restaurant since 1979. Offers a wide variety of sub sandwiches. Many locations around the area.
  • People’s Kitchen: $20-30 per person, comfort foods & craft cocktails served amid colorful industrial decor, plus weekend brunch.
  • Ruckus Ramen: $10-20 per person, unique take on East Asian cuisine located within The Avenue bar on the Eastside of Lansing.
  • Soup Spoon Cafe: $10-20 per person, full service restaurant and bar known for their ‘scratch’ kitchen and craft cocktails.


Downtown

  • EnVie: $20-30 per person, a bistro in the heart of Lansing’s downtown area with a rotating menu. Open Tuesday through Saturday for dinner only.
  • Golden Harvest: $10-20 per person, legendary grungy breakfast joint in Lansing. Cash only.
  • Lansing Shuffle: Food hall with ~7 different cuisines represented, on the Grand River in downtown Lansing


Old Town

  • Meat Southern BBQ and Carnivore Cuisine: $10-20 per person, local BBQ joint with kitschy interior. There can be a wait.
  • The Cosmos: $10-20 per person. Wood-fired pizza with a connected full bar, Zoobie’s Old Town Tavern, in Lansing’s Old Town neighborhood.


Westside Lansing

  • Horrocks Farm Market: $10-20 per person, has gelato, beer, wine bar, sushi and other pre-made food. Located within Lansing’s quintessential farm market. Started in 1959 as a road-side fruit stand, this market has grown and evolved over the years. Has a beer garden nestled in their outdoor plant market which often hosts local events.
  • Ohana Sushi: $30-40 per person, all-you-can-eat sushi made with fresh and, when possible, local ingredients.

Local Guide Map

Where to Drink

Coffee
Bars and Breweries
Coffee

Find these great coffee spots in downtown East Lansing.

  • Foster Coffee Company: a Michigan-based coffee shop is housed within a modern/industrial design space.
  • Haraz Coffee House: Yemeni coffee shop and bakery with locations across the country.
  • Koala Tea & Coffee: Milk tea and bubble tea with baked goods. Their Okemos location has a robot that will deliver your food to you.
  • Moka & Co.: Yemeni specialty coffee shop with incredible baked goods.
  • Strange Matter: Woman-owned local coffee bar and bakery that is very active in the community. There are three locations in the area, with the closest being in MSU’s Union building. Known for their donuts and pastries, their vegan gluten-free donuts are beloved.
Bars and Breweries
  • Beggar’s Banquet: $$, local American food restaurant and pub founded in 1973
  • Crunchy’s Burgers and Beers: $10-20 per person. Local American food restaurant and pub founded in 1982. Home to one of the area’s best burgers and its specialty “bucket of beer”.
  • Hopcat: $10-20 per person. A trendy Michigan-based chain bar
  • Jolly Pumpkin: $10-20 per person. Known for their sour beer. Serves burgers, pizza, and other pub staples.
  • Peanut Barrel: $$, local American food restaurant and pub founded in 1973
  • The Avenue: Set in the heart of Lansing’s eastside neighborhood, The Ave is home to Ruckus Ramen, pinball, pool and live music. LGBTQ+ safe space with mocktail options.

Explore Lansing

Where to Visit
What to Do
Where to Visit

Broad Museum: Housed in a spectacular building designed by Pritzker Prize-winning “starchitect” Zaha Hadid, the MSU Broad Museum boasts collection strengths in Greek and Roman antiquities; Mesoamerican sculptures and vessels; North American and European sculpture, prints, photographs, and paintings; and works in a variety of media from different African, Asian, Latin American, and Middle Eastern cultures. These collections are showcased in the CORE (Center for Object Research and Engagement), which offers unique opportunities to view, reflect on, and investigate art objects spanning 5,000 years of human history. Hours 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM, Wednesday-Sunday; admission free with online registration, available here: https://broadmuseum.msu.edu/visit/getting-here/ 

Garden tour – botanical, children’s: The Beal Botanical Garden offers free tours open to the public. Established in 1873, the W. J. Beal Botanical Garden is the oldest, continuously operated university botanical garden in the United States and illuminates the interconnectedness between people, plants, and place. This living laboratory encourages learning and exploration of the natural world.

Dairy Store: ​​Enjoy ice cream and cheese at the MSU Dairy Store, open Tuesdays-Sundays from 12-8 p.m.

Capitol tour: The Michigan Capitol is open to visitors Monday through Friday. Guided tours are available between 9:00 and 4:00.

Old Town: Old town offers unique experiences through special events and eclectic shops.

Curious Book Shop: The thinking person’s visit to East Lansing wouldn’t be complete without a browse through the three floors of new and used titles at Curious! Check out their layout at http://www.curiousbooks.com/layout.html and make a special effort to get there if you’re into Oziana, rare sci-fi and fantasy, or vintage magazines. After all, you’ll need something to read on the plane home, right? Open Sunday 12 PM – 5 PM, Monday-Saturday 10 AM – 7 PM, and yes, they validate parking!

Potter Park Zoo: This AZA accredited zoo has been around since 1920 and sits on the Lansing River Trail. Known for its otter exhibit and conservation education, Potter Park Zoo is a beloved part of the community. 

Abrams Planetarium: Shows for the public are on Friday and Saturday nights and Sunday afternoons

Note that the MSU Museum will be closed for 18 months beginning in July.

What to Do

Bike tours (MSU Bikes and Renova Bikes): Enjoy the Lansing River trail which goes through MSU’s campus on a bicycle. A great way to explore the area as you follow the Red Cedar River and Grand River as it meanders through East Lansing and Lansing.

 

Lansing Lugnuts baseball game: Lansing’s very own minor league baseball team. The stadium has outfield lawn seats which but up against a kid’s play area, making baseball games fun for the whole family.

 

The Robin Theatre: Located in Lansing’s historical REO town, this local theatre/book store hosts something for everyone. The theatre is located within a 100-year old store front and provides an intimate environment for enjoying an eclectic array of performances, from film festivals to poetry readings.


Bands in Town: Find out about live music happenings in town. Includes local and touring musicians.

Meet Our Gold Sponsors

AM Quartex is the 2024 Lanyard Sponsor!

AM Quartex

AM’s digital collections and technology platforms enrich the study, research and teaching of primary sources. AM works with libraries, archives and heritage institutions to digitise the world’s historical and cultural knowledge. Developed to present AM's own primary source collections, Quartex helps customers bring archival materials to life.

Follow them on  X @adammatthewgrp and LinkedIn. 

Visit Their Website /*! elementor - v3.23.0 - 15-07-2024 */ .elementor-widget-image{text-align:center}.elementor-widget-image a{display:inline-block}.elementor-widget-image a img[src$=".svg"]{width:48px}.elementor-widget-image img{vertical-align:middle;display:inline-block}

4Science

At 4Science, we lead the charge in advocating Open Science as lead contributor to DSpace worldwide. As a DSpace Certified Platinum Provider, Certified ORCID Service Provider, Cloud Security Alliance Trusted provider, ISO 27001, and ISO 9001 certified company, we ensure the highest level of assurance.

Expertise Highlights: With over two decades of experience, our team is an authoritative source on technological, methodological, and policy-related repository issues. We’ve pioneered DSpace features such as ORCID integration, COAR-NGR technologies, NOTIFY innovation, and Machine Learning for PDF recognition.

Comprehensive Solutions: Specializing in Research Information Management Systems (RIMS), Research Data Management (RDM), and digital cultural heritage management, we offer turnkey solutions for DSpace, DSpace extensions (DSpace-CRIS and DSpace-GLAM), and Dataverse.

Guiding Advanced Implementations: We guide our clients in implementing advanced modules for enhanced repository experiences, ensuring interoperability, global connectedness, and robust security.

Adherence to Standards: Our solutions align with international standards and policies such as OpenAIRE, ORCID, IIIF, Open Access, Open Science, Research Impact, and Digital Preservation.

Follow them on X @4ScienceIT and on LinkedIn.

Visit Their Website

Meet Our Silver Sponsors

TIND is the 2024 Swag Sponsor!

TIND

TIND has developed the TIND Digital Archive, a tool to showcase and preserve any digital collection, including photographs, books, manuscripts, newspapers, and audiovisual material.

TIND is an official CERN spin-off providing commercial library management systems, digital preservation, and research data management solutions based on CERN open-source software. Serving academic, public, and special research libraries around the globe, TIND is headquartered in Oslo, Norway.

Follow them on X @tind_io and LinkedIn. 

Visit Their Website

Wiki Education

Wiki Education is a non-profit that envisions a world in which students, scholars, scientists, archivists, librarians, and other members of academic and cultural institutions are actively engaged in sharing their knowledge with the general public through Wikipedia, Wikidata, and other open collaboration projects on the web.

Follow them on X @wikieducation and LinkedIn. 

Visit Their Website

East View Information Services

East View is a full-service library vendor for over 30 years with an expanding list of offerings that extends across borders, languages and ideologies in the vernacular languages of the source. Uncommon information from extraordinary places, with exceptional service.

Follow them on X @eastviewpeeps and LinkedIn. 

Visit Their Website

Recollect CMS

Recollect's industry-leading Collection Management System ensures you have the tools you need to fully manage your digital collection and engage your community.

Our cloud-based platform enhances your collections with features such as crowd-sourcing and a flexible metadata scheme - along with optional preservation and exhibition functionality.

Follow them on LinkedIn. 

Visit Their Website

LOCKSS

The LOCKSS Program at Stanford Libraries provides open-source technologies and services for high-confidence, resilient, secure digital preservation. Since 1999, the "Lots of Copies Keep Stuff Safe" approach--and the LOCKSS Program's award-winning open source software--has provided the foundation for robust digital preservation of all types of digital content for libraries, publishers, memory institutions, content creators and cultural stewards. We address comprehensive threats to data persistence; deliver reliable service and support; and foster a community of self-determined digital preservation practitioners. We have a long track record of leadership in digital preservation and count as partners many of the world’s leading memory institutions. Learn more about LOCKSS at lockss.org.

Follow them on X @LOCKSS and LinkedIn.

Visit Their Website
